lines.watchItem: Cloud and AI customers raised their 2026 spending plans sharply, and TSMC's July sales and lifted full-year guidance track that pull. Watch whether these order signals hold as leading-edge wafer plans get set for 2027.

Advanced packaging still gates how many accelerators reach customers, with lines booked into 2027 and waits of roughly a year to a year and a half. The gap between packaging demand and capacity is narrowing but has not closed.

Three customers hold more than 85 percent of advanced-packaging output, and one of them holds about 60 percent. A slowdown at that single account would leave packaging capacity that is hard to refill quickly.

Stacked memory now caps accelerator output more tightly than packaging does, with one major supplier covering only about half of requested volume and NVIDIA trimming memory per chip on its next flagship. Packaging slots filled today can sit idle if the memory does not arrive alongside them.

Custom accelerators designed for cloud operators are growing far faster than merchant GPUs, Microsoft is negotiating capacity for hundreds of thousands of in-house chips, and MediaTek has raised its share target. The leading-node customer base is drifting from two GPU vendors toward a wider set of custom-chip programs.

TSMC posted a 67.7 percent gross margin with 2026 revenue growth guided above 40 percent, and Samsung raised advanced contract chipmaking prices 10 to 15 percent. Memory suppliers are taking a growing share of AI-server profit at the same time, so pricing strength across the chain is uneven.

Intel's bridge packaging landed a multi-million-unit order from Google and targets high-volume output in 2027 at roughly half the cost, while Samsung and outside assembly houses quote much shorter waits than TSMC. That route carries its own limits: a single fully booked capacitor supplier and a design better matched to custom chips than to high-bandwidth GPUs.

NVIDIA's China data-center revenue has fallen to roughly nothing and Beijing has told licensed customers to keep the hardware in Hong Kong, while a rising share of accelerator demand rests on vendor credit and outside capital platforms. Watch whether that credit-supported demand keeps converting into wafer and packaging orders.
